bullets.title: CRWV: Strong Q2 beats on power capacity and backlog; multiple PT raises; +16-19% pre-market
bullets.body: CoreWeave exceeded consensus active power (>1.5 GW vs 1.25 GW est.), reported $104.2B backlog with $7.4B Q2 bookings and >$25B signed early Q3. EBITDA margin 58.6% vs 55.8% consensus; managed inference ARR expected to reach $250M+ by year-end from ~$1M baseline. JPMorgan raised PT to $120 (from $110, Neutral) and Mizuho raised PT to $115 (from $100, Neutral); Piper Sandler also raised PT. Stock surged 16-19% premarket though Hedgeye flagged revenue per watt at new low of $1.7 and adjusted net losses +334% YoY.

bullets.title: NBIS: Massive Q2 beat — EBITDA $236M vs $169M est.; raises power target to 5 GW by 2027
bullets.body: Nebius Q2 revenue $582.3M beat estimates ($570M); adj. EBITDA margin 40.6% vs 29.6% est.; gross margin 77.1% vs 68.1% est. New contracts signed at $40-50M/MW for short-term capacity. FY26 revenue guidance reiterated at $3.0-3.4B; CapEx $20-25B; run rate revenue target $7-9B. Stock +17% premarket. Revenue +454% YoY.

bullets.title: SMCI: Best quarterly gross margin in 3+ years (17.6%); JPM raises PT to $45 from $32; +9% pre-market
bullets.body: Super Micro posted best quarterly gross margin in 3+ years at 17.6% vs 15.8% consensus and guided FY27 revenue $65-72B (+75% YoY). JP Morgan raised price target to $45 from $32. ITC action from NLST (Roth raises PT to $15, Buy) names Supermicro as an additional respondent in Micron DRAM patent case.

bullets.title: LITE: Pulls forward $1.25B revenue target by 2 quarters on OCS ramp; +8.6% pre-market
bullets.body: Lumentum pulled forward its $1.25B revenue target to the September quarter, two quarters ahead of schedule, driven by OCS ramp and pump laser pricing strength. Strong CPO commentary drove a +8-9% premarket move. Supplier AXTI +9.9%, COHR +7.3%, CIEN +6.5% in sympathy.

bullets.title: NVDA: Hon Hai 54% YoY revenue beat signals robust AI hardware demand; stock +1.2% pre-market; optics shift to NVL576 in 2027
bullets.body: Foxconn (Hon Hai) — key Nvidia and Apple supplier — reported revenue up 54.2% YoY to $29.4B and net income of $1.9B, beating $1.8B estimates, signaling robust AI hardware demand. NVDA +1.2% premarket, biggest Mag 7 gainer. Separately, sources note NVDA content is shifting from memories to optics with NVL576 expected higher adoption in 2027, a positive read for MRVL and SMCI. SOX valuations at 27x forward P/E suggest worst of pullback may be behind.

bullets.title: CLS: Bullish NDR — F'27 $35B revenue, F'28 $47B+; $3.5B equity raise from strength
bullets.body: Celestica management expressed high confidence in demand into Q3/Q4 with multi-year visibility to 2028-29. F'27 revenue forecasted at $35B and F'28 at $47B (>30% growth), with internal demand signals tracking above consensus. Supply constraints (memory 52 weeks, specialty silicon up to 100 weeks) provide ~1-year visibility. $3.5B equity raise covers 2027 with no additional raise anticipated through 2028; 55% ROIC last quarter. CLS.CN +6.8% on Canadian exchange.

bullets.title: AAPL: Hedgeye bearish — smallest revenue beat since Sept 2025; China miss, Sept guidance below consensus
bullets.body: Hedgeye maintains a short view: AAPL's Sept quarter guidance of 9-11% growth is below consensus ~12%; gross margin guidance 47-48% is weak at 48% ex-tariff refunds. China revenue missed consensus by 4% with Huawei pressure intensifying. iPhone growth expected to decelerate for several quarters. Memory costs rising, adding margin pressure.

bullets.title: TSLA: China domestic sales -32% YoY/-47% MoM in July; exports surge +143% YoY
bullets.body: Tesla domestic Chinese insurance retail sales fell 32% YoY and 47% MoM to 27,756 units in July 2026, losing 3.1ppt BEV share to BYD. However, wholesale reached 93,579 units (+38% YoY) and exports surged to 66,330 units (+143% YoY, +83% MoM). Morgan Stanley intern survey shows Tesla as most desired car brand at 6% (up from 5%) but robotaxi preference lags Waymo and Uber.

bullets.title: AMD: Server CPU TAM projected at $200B+ by 2030; Radeon RX 9000 GPU prices raised up to 20%
bullets.body: AMD stated it expects the server CPU market to surpass $200B by 2030, signaling significant TAM expansion. On the GPU side, AMD officially raised Radeon RX 9000 series prices by up to 20%, with the RX 9070 XT now exceeding $1,000. Intel's Razor Lake-AX halo-class SoC confirmed in development targeting AMD competition around 2028.

bullets.title: SNOW: 52-week high at $339.60, +77.1% YTD; APP at 52-week low, -32.6% YTD
bullets.body: Snowflake hit a 52-week high at $339.60 (+1.6% on the day, +77.1% YTD) while AppLovin touched a 52-week low at $313.90 (-1.5%, -32.6% YTD) per StreetAccount's 52-week highs/lows report covering 103 highs and 26 lows.

bullets.title: IONQ/QBTS/RGTI: Jefferies bullish on quantum sector; 2027 as key inflection year
bullets.body: Jefferies highlights QNT as top pick with BUY at $85 PT (FY26 guidance raised to $30M revenue, $81M YTD bookings). IONQ cited as most ambitious platform with exposure across computing, networking, cybersecurity. QBTS improving commercial adoption; RGTI a 'prove-it' story. 2027 set as inflection year when ~100 logical-qubit systems begin solving production workloads; 2029 bigger TAM unlock. Trump administration backing $2B federal quantum program.

bullets.title: DKNG: Indiana July sports betting handle +35% YoY; DKNG handle +31% with 36% market share
bullets.body: Indiana July sports betting GGR rose 16% YoY with handle +35% YoY. DraftKings July GGR +12% YoY, handle +31% YoY, market share 36% but hold rate compressed 180bps YoY to 10.3%. FanDuel GGR +19%, BetMGM +31%, Fanatics +32%. CZR GGR -16% YoY. Morgan Stanley notes online sports betting volumes/users accelerated on World Cup but margins pressured by promotions.

bullets.title: HIMS: Hedgeye moves to short bench; CAC, LTV, and cash flow moving in wrong direction
bullets.body: Hedgeye moved HIMS to its short bench after mixed 2Q26 results featuring back-end-loaded guidance; customer acquisition costs, lifetime value metrics, and cash flow are all deteriorating. The new AI investment strategy lacks fundamental support per Hedgeye's analysis.

bullets.title: BE/CEG/GEV: Texas data center audit creates BTM opportunity; Amazon withdraws CEG Maryland plans
bullets.body: Texas Gov. Abbott's 40-60 day data center audit creates a quasi-moratorium, with risks of spreading to other states. Behind-the-meter players including BE and SEI seen as beneficiaries from grid constraints, while IPPs NRG and VST face headwinds. Amazon separately withdrew its CEG Maryland data center plans. NRG's $2,700/kW new Texas power plants are seen as supportive for GEV pricing.

bullets.title: FSLR/ENPH: First Solar upgraded on tariff clarity; Goldman raises data center power demand 170% by 2030
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs raised its global data center power demand growth estimate 2025-2030 to 170% from 117% prior, with most power expected from natural gas and renewables. First Solar was upgraded to outperform on Section 232 tariffs adding pricing clarity. NexTracker and Array Technologies expected to face near-term pressure from tariffs.

bullets.title: TTWO: Citi maintains Buy at $270 PT; GTA VI presales strong ahead of Nov 19 launch
bullets.body: Take-Two reported F1Q27 bookings and non-GAAP EPS above consensus. FY27 bookings guidance of $8.0-8.2B is 6% below Street midpoint and non-GAAP EPS guidance of $5.75-6.00 is 19% below consensus. GTA VI showing strong presales ahead of its November 19 release; Citi PT $270 implies ~26x FY28 earnings with Buy rating maintained.

bullets.title: MDB/MSFT/CRWV: Wolfe SaaS digest highlights MSFT Maia 300 chip scaling; SaaS indices recovering
bullets.body: Wolfe Research notes MSFT plans to scale Maia 300 chip production. All-SaaS index at 5.7x FY+2 EV/Sales, up 8.26% WoW; All-Security index 8.6x, up 6.77%; All-Vertical 6.1x, up 8.59%. IGV returned -2.8% YTD vs S&P 500 +14.0%. Software names including CRM, INTU, HUBS, NOW, TEAM, PLTR, SHOP down 1.5-3% on profit-taking per pre-market flow.

bullets.title: ETSY: Raises FY26 GMV guidance to mid-single digit; $2B buyback authorized
bullets.body: Etsy raised FY26 GMV growth guidance to mid-single digit from prior low-single digit on ML investment and mobile app momentum (mobile GMV outpacing overall). Company divested Depop and reduced headcount by 220 while planning to rehire 100+ in tech roles. $2B new buyback authorization announced; no major M&A planned.

bullets.title: July CPI in-line: core +0.22% MoM, headline +0.07% MoM; Fed hold thesis intact through year-end
bullets.body: July core CPI rose 0.22% MoM (vs ~0.23-0.24% estimates) and headline +0.07% MoM. Core PCE tracking 20bps, down 3bps from earlier estimates. Rent and OER both +0.3%; core goods bounced sharply; lodging weak at -2.75%. Multiple strategists note data does not materially strengthen tightening case; September rate decision remains near coin-toss with August data still pending. CTAs are record short bonds (~$300M P&L per 1bp in 10Y yields), creating covering risk on benign prints.

bullets.title: NVDA: $500B AI-factory financing structure scrutinized; China chip dumping risk to collateral values
bullets.body: NVDA's $500B AI-factory buildout with PE firms (BLK, BX, BAM, APO, KKR, GS) initially widened credit spreads until CEO clarified support capped at ~25% per project. China chip ramping creates 'capacity dumping' risk lowering collateral valuations backing data-center ABS. CME launching H100/B200 compute futures on Oct 5. ERCOT lowered FY27 power demand forecast, and Wood Mackenzie estimates only ~28% of 1.07TW requested capacity will materialize.
